text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- The labour and social welfare minister Joso Skara annouces a big clearup among social security card holders, as many of them are fit to work.
- Osijek and Mohacs in Hungary have been reconnected by a bus line passing over Croatian territory still controlled by Serbs.
- The identification of the Ovcara mass grave victims in Zagreb has been taken over by Croatian experts from U.N.

- A London-based firm Partners in Hospitality has put together a feasibility study on the reconstruction of Dubrovnik's hotels. Investment in hotels Imperial, Libertas, Excelsior, Argentina and Belvedere seen at a minimum $10 million.
- A suspended Supreme Court president, Krunislav Olujic, hospitalised for heart trouble. The debate on his dismissal by the members of the State Judicial Council postponed until January 9.
- Some 50 in 500 builders taking part in reconstruction projects in the war-ravaged areas have failed the quality test by the reconstruction and development ministry.
- The law is on the side of those who refuse to pay Croatian Radio Television's (HRT) monthly service fee, says Ivo Skrabalo, one of the initiators of the boycott.
- Zagreb's tram service (ZET) workers' trade union has rejected a proposed corporate employment agreement. A strike is not being ruled out. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
